title: Maximal-velocity deficit under a finite-support constraint in hard-wall half-line continuous-time quantum walk
abstract: Continuous-time quantum walks on a lattice spread ballistically and converge to a limiting distribution for the rescaled position. On the hard-wall half line the boundary reflects the walker but does not change the bulk dispersion, so the ballistic front remains set by the maximal group velocity. We ask how close one can get to this front when the initial state is constrained to occupy only the first $M$ sites. We show that optimizing the moment-generating function of the limiting-velocity distribution over this finite-support class reduces to the principal eigenvalue of an explicit $M\times M$ Hermitian matrix, which yields the optimal state by direct diagonalization. For large $M$, a near-front scaling limit produces a continuum description that controls the entire peak region. In particular, the maximal mean drift approaches the front with an inverse-square deficit in $M$ and a constant prefactor $π^2/4$. Numerical results verify both the finite-$M$ spectral formulation and the predicted scaling.
summary: This paper investigates the speed limit of a quantum walker confined to a half-line lattice by constraining its initial state to $M$ sites. It shows that the maximal achievable drift velocity approaches the theoretical maximum with a predictable, inverse-square deficit scaling with $M$. The methodology involves advanced spectral analysis, moving from finite matrices to a continuum operator limit.
main_problem: The paper determines how close the maximal mean drift velocity of a continuous-time quantum walk (CTQW) on a hard-wall half-line can approach the theoretical maximal front speed when the initial state is restricted to a finite number of sites ($M$).
main_result: The maximal mean drift velocity exhibits a deficit that decays with an inverse-square dependence on $M$, with the continuum limit yielding a constant prefactor of $\pi^2/4$.
method: The analysis uses moment-generating functions and spectral theory, reducing the optimization problem to finding the largest eigenvalue of explicit, finite-dimensional Hermitian matrices, which is then analyzed in the continuum limit.
model_or_system: The system is a continuous-time quantum walk (CTQW) evolving on the hard-wall half-line ($\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$) governed by a nearest-neighbor Hamiltonian. The dynamics are analyzed using the sine transform and weak-limit theorems.
key_observables: Maximal mean drift velocity ($	ext{vmax}(M)$), asymptotic velocity random variable ($V$), and the moment-generating function ($G_\psi(s)$).
important_parameters: Finite support size $M$, the bulk dispersion velocity ($2J$), and the continuum scaling variable $u$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on stationary-phase estimates and the validity of weak-limit theorems for CTQWs, particularly in the large-$M$ limit.
figures_summary: The notes do not provide a summary of figures, but mention numerical verification of both the finite-$M$ spectral formulation and the predicted scaling.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the system and establishing the bulk limit, then characterizing the finite-$M$ spectral problem via matrix diagonalization, followed by deriving the continuum scaling limit, and finally extracting the constant prefactor.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous spectral methods to analyze transport phenomena in quantum systems constrained by boundaries, connecting discrete spectral problems to continuous field theory limits.
